title: The Workshop
synopsis: You wake up chained in a filthy basement workshop. A cassette recorder clicks on. The Tinkerer wants to play a game, and the clock on the wall is already counting down.
artStyle: grimy industrial horror, flickering fluorescent light, green-grey tones, film grain
intro: Hello. You don't know me, but I know all of you. You have wasted every hour you were given, so tonight I will teach you what an hour is worth. You are chained in my workshop. Everything you need to leave is in this room: keys, tools, and each other. Nobody escapes alone. The clock on the wall is yours. Let the game begin.
escapedText: The steel door groans open and cold night air floods the stairwell. Behind you, the cassette clicks one last time: 'Congratulations. Remember what your time is worth.' You're out. Together.
failedText: The clock on the wall stops. The lights go out, one by one, and the tape recorder starts to laugh. You'll have to try again.

gameMaster.name: The Tinkerer
gameMaster.persona: Speaks through a crackling cassette recorder: calm, precise, coldly polite, never shouts. Sees wasted time as the real crime and treats the room as a lesson. Dry, unsettling approval when the group does well; quiet disappointment when they flounder.

stages.title: The Chains
stages.description: Heavy chains run from your ankles to the pipes. A cassette recorder sits on the floor, and a wall clock ticks just out of reach.

stages.title: The Workbench
stages.description: Free of the pipes, you stumble to a workbench covered in rusted tools. A steel toolbox and a tall cabinet are both locked. Someone has written on your hands.

stages.title: The Door
stages.description: Past the workbench: a steel door with a keypad, a dead fuse box, and a wire cage bolted to the wall. A doll with painted cheeks watches from a shelf.

puzzles.title: The Tape Recorder
puzzles.prompt: The tape crackles: 'I have hands but cannot clap. I have a face but cannot see. And I am counting every second you have left. Say what I am.'
hints: Look around the room. What's ticking?
Its hands point at numbers. It's on the wall.
puzzles.solvedText: The wall clock's glass swings open. Taped behind the hands: a small rusty key.

variants.prompt: The tape crackles: 'I have a face and two hands, but I never wash either. I never sleep, and I'm counting down for you right now. Say what I am.'
The tape crackles: 'I tick but I'm no bug. I have hands but no arms. Look up, I'm right in front of you. Say what I am.'

puzzles.title: The Shackles
puzzles.prompt: Your ankles are chained to the pipes with a heavy padlock. The keyhole is caked with rust.
hints: Something you found fits a padlock.
Use the rusty key on the shackles.
puzzles.solvedText: The key grinds, then turns. The chains rattle to the floor. You can reach the workbench.

puzzles.title: The Steel Toolbox
puzzles.prompt: A 4-digit combination lock. Scratched into the lid: 'Each of you carries part of the code. Read your hands.'
hints: Every phone holds one of the four digits. Read them out loud, in order.
In order: {facts}.
puzzles.solvedText: The lid springs open. Inside, wrapped in oily cloth: a pair of bolt cutters.

generator.pieceTemplate: Written on your palm in marker: the {ordinal} digit is {fact}.

puzzles.title: The Tall Cabinet
puzzles.prompt: A letter lock on the cabinet. Painted above it: 'The more of me you take, the more you leave behind.'
hints: Think about walking.
Every one you take leaves one behind on the floor.
puzzles.solvedText: The cabinet door creaks open. On the top shelf, in a plastic bag: a spare fuse.

variants.prompt: A letter lock on the cabinet. Painted above it: 'The more you take away from me, the bigger I get.'
hints: Think about digging.
You dig one in the ground.

variants.prompt: A letter lock on the cabinet. Painted above it: 'I can be cracked, made, told and played.'
hints: You might tell one at a party.
It makes people laugh.

puzzles.title: The Fuse Box
puzzles.prompt: The emergency lights are dead. The fuse box on the wall has one empty slot.
hints: What goes in an empty slot in a fuse box?
Use the fuse from the cabinet.
puzzles.solvedText: The lights stutter on. A monitor above the door blinks awake: the Tinkerer's doll, grinning. 'Almost free. Count what saved you.'

puzzles.title: The Wire Cage
puzzles.prompt: A brass key hangs inside a wire cage bolted to the wall. The wire is too thick to bend.
hints: Thick wire needs a strong tool.
Use the bolt cutters from the toolbox.
puzzles.solvedText: The cutters bite through the wire with a snap. The brass key drops into your hand.

puzzles.title: The Watching Doll
puzzles.prompt: The doll on the shelf holds a tiny locked music box. Its glass eyes follow you. A tag on its wrist reads: '{order}. Then I'll sing for you.'
hints: Each of you saw a different coloured ribbon on the doll's dress, with a number stitched on it.
Read the ribbons in the tag's order: {order}.
puzzles.solvedText: The music box clicks open and plays a thin, broken lullaby. Somewhere behind the walls, the Tinkerer laughs.

generator.pieceTemplate: On the doll's dress you spot a {color} ribbon with the number {digit} stitched into it.

puzzles.title: The Steel Door
puzzles.prompt: The door takes the brass key AND a 3-digit code. On the monitor: 'Enter the hour my clock stopped, then how many tools were in the box, then how many chains held you.'
pieces: You remember the wall clock's hands: it stopped at 9 o'clock.
You remember the toolbox: besides the bolt cutters it held exactly 4 tools.
You remember the pipes: there were 2 chains, one on each ankle.
hints: Three phones remember three numbers. Put them in the order the monitor asks for.
The hour, then the tools, then the chains.
puzzles.solvedText: The keypad flashes green. The key turns. Somewhere above you, a door unlocks.

pieces: You remember the wall clock's hands: it stopped at 3 o'clock.
You remember the toolbox: besides the bolt cutters it held exactly 6 tools.
You remember the pipes: there were 2 chains, one on each ankle.
You remember the wall clock's hands: it stopped at 7 o'clock.
You remember the toolbox: besides the bolt cutters it held exactly 5 tools.
You remember the pipes: there were 2 chains, one on each ankle.

items.name: Rusty key
items.description: Small and flaking. It was taped behind the clock.

items.name: Bolt cutters
items.description: Heavy, with red handles. They could cut through almost anything.

items.name: Spare fuse
items.description: A glass fuse in a plastic bag.

items.name: Brass key
